counterexample: Take edges in relaxation order (s,a) of weight 1, (a,b) of weight 1, and (s,b) of weight 10. During the first in-place Bellman–Ford pass, dist[a] becomes 1 and then dist[b] becomes 2. Yet the shortest s-to-b path with at most one edge has length 10. Thus after k=1, dist[b] is not the claimed restricted shortest-path length.
